name: ACCUS (FIA national sporting authority for the USA)
scope: national ASN liaison to the FIA
notes: Formed 1957; members IMSA, IndyCar, NASCAR, NHRA, SCCA, USAC. Issues FIA international licences: grade A (<=1 kg/hp cars), B (1-2 kg/hp; age 18+ and ~10 sanctioned races in 2 yrs), C (2-3 kg/hp), D (>3 kg/hp, club/bronze international series). Co-sanctions F4 U.S. and FR Americas for FIA status (super licence points).

name: All Star Circuit of Champions
scope: regional/national 410 winged sprint tour (Midwest/East)
notes: Owned by Tony Stewart 2015-2023; acquired by High Limit (Larson/Sweet) after 2023; revived 2025 operated by Rich Farmer.

name: Andersen Promotions (USF Pro Championships)
scope: national promoter/owner of the USF Pro Championships ladder (USF Juniors, USF2000, USF Pro 2000)
notes: Dan Andersen co-founded US F2000 in 1990 and revived it in 2010; took over Star Mazda (renamed Pro Mazda) in Dec 2012. Series are USAC-sanctioned and owned/managed by Andersen Promotions. Ladder formerly branded Road to Indy / Mazda Road to Indy. >USD 29M in scholarships awarded since inception.

name: Automobile Racing Club of America
scope: national + regional (East, West)
notes: Founded 1953 in Toledo as MARC, renamed ARCA 1964; bought by NASCAR April 2018; from 2020 runs ARCA Menards Series plus East/West (former K&N Pro Series East/West).

name: American Speed Association (Track Enterprises era)
scope: regional/national pavement super late model tours (ASA STARS National, ASA Midwest Tour, ASA Southern Super Series, ASA/CRA Super Series)
notes: Original ASA dates from 1968 (general knowledge, low); revived brand under Track Enterprises (Bob Sargent) sanctions STARS National Tour from 2023 and aligned regional tours.

name: American Sprint Car Series
scope: national + 9 regional 360/410/non-wing sprint series
notes: National Tour 34-35 races/yr; DIRTcar affiliated rules.

name: CARS Racing Tour (Competition Auto Racing Series)
scope: regional Southeast late model tours (Late Model Stock, Pro Late Model)
notes: Lineage from Hooters Pro Cup/USAR (1995); two-division CARS Tour since 2015; owned since 2023 by Dale Earnhardt Jr., Jeff Burton, Kevin Harvick, Trackhouse; Speedway Motorsports joined 2026.

name: Championship Auto Racing Teams / Champ Car (OWRS)
scope: national/international top-level open wheel (historic)
notes: Team-owner-run body formed Nov 1978 after split from USAC; sanctioned 1979-2003; Champ Car World Series (Open Wheel Racing Series) 2004-2007; merged into IRL/IndyCar 22 Feb 2008. Ran Indy Lights (to 2001) and used Atlantic as feeder (2002-2008).

name: Champion Racing Association
scope: regional Midwest pavement late models (ASA/CRA Super Series SLM, JEGS/CRA All-Stars crate tour)
notes: Super Series began 1997; JEGS/CRA All-Stars crate tour founded 2011 with Chevrolet Performance.

name: Federation Internationale de l'Automobile
scope: international
notes: Owns the Driver Categorisation (Platinum/Gold/Silver/Bronze) used by IMSA, SRO and one-make cups to define pro-am lineups; FIA F4/Formula Regional/F3/F2 ladder; super licence points system.

name: Grand American Road Racing Association
scope: national pro sports-car (historic)
notes: NASCAR-affiliated sanctioning body of the Rolex Sports Car Series (2000-2013) and Grand-Am Cup/KONI/Continental Tire Challenge; merged with IMSA/ALMS for 2014.

name: High Limit Racing
scope: national 410 winged sprint tour
notes: Founded by Kyle Larson and Brad Sweet; 2024 points fund $1M, champion $250k.

name: International Kart Federation
scope: national (historically west-coast) karting
notes: First US karting organisation (California, rules published Nov 1957); Grand Nationals; allied with SKUSA in 2018.

name: International Motor Contest Association
scope: weekly dirt track sanction, Midwest/South/West US
notes: Classes: Modified, Late Model, SportMod (Northern/Southern), Stock Car, Hobby Stock, Sport Compact, Sprint, Mod Lite. Minimum age 14 in Sport Compact/Hobby/SportMod (14-15 need resume). Founding year 1915 from general knowledge (low).

name: International Motor Sports Association
scope: national pro sports-car sanctioning body
notes: Founded 1969 by John and Peggy Bishop with Bill France Sr. financing; merged with Grand-Am (Sept 2012, effective 2014); owned by NASCAR Holdings. Sanctions WeatherTech SportsCar Championship, Michelin Pilot Challenge, VP Racing SportsCar Challenge, Mazda MX-5 Cup, Porsche Carrera Cup NA, Lamborghini Super Trofeo NA and Ferrari Challenge NA. IMSA driver membership minimum age 17 (15 for MX-5 Cup), reducible by one year at IMSA discretion.

name: INDYCAR LLC (IndyCar / Indy Racing League)
scope: national (top-level open wheel); sanctions IndyCar Series and Indy NXT
notes: Created by IMS owner Tony George as Indy Racing League (first season 1996) to rival CART; absorbed Champ Car in Feb 2008; owned by Penske Entertainment since 2020. Self-sanctions IndyCar and Indy NXT; issues IndyCar licences (new objective licensing criteria from 2027).

name: INEX (Legends/Bandolero/Thunder Roadster sanctioning)
scope: national/international spec-car sanction (Legends, Bandolero, Thunder Roadster)
notes: Sanctioning arm for US Legend Cars International products; divisions Bandits 7-11, Outlaws 12+, Young Lions 10-15, Semi-Pro 16+, Pro, Masters 40+.

name: Lucas Oil Late Model Dirt Series (FloSports)
scope: national super dirt late model tour
notes: Founded 2004 as NARA by Spencer Wilson; Lucas Oil from 2005; FloSports bought end of 2025.

name: National Auto Sport Association
scope: national amateur club racing via regional chapters; HPDE, time trial, wheel-to-wheel racing
notes: Founded 1991 around track days; HPDE groups 1-4 lead to a competition licence; National Championships since 2006 (Daytona since 2021). Popular classes Spec Miata, Spec E30, 944 Spec. Membership ~USD 45/yr.

name: National Association for Stock Car Auto Racing
scope: national + regional + weekly local (NASCAR Local Racing Series, formerly Weekly Series)
notes: Sanctions Cup, O'Reilly Auto Parts (ex-Xfinity) and Craftsman Truck national series, the Whelen Modified Tour, ARCA (owned since 2018) and the weekly local track program; also NASCAR Youth Series quarter midgets (ex-USAC .25).

name: NASCAR Youth Series (formerly USAC .25)
scope: national youth quarter midget sanction
notes: Per Wikipedia the former USAC .25 quarter midget sanction is now NASCAR Youth Series; transition year not verified.

name: Parella Motorsports Holdings / SpeedTour (Racing America)
scope: national promoter (vintage, Trans Am, junior formula)
notes: Owns SVRA, Trans Am, FR Americas, F4 U.S., Ligier Junior Formula Championship and IGT; SpeedTour festivals; acquired Racing America Dec 2025 and rebranded under that name.

name: Pro All Stars Series
scope: regional Northeast + South super late model, NE modifieds
notes: Founded 2001 by Tom Mayberry; runs Oxford Plains Speedway (bought 2012) and Oxford 250.

name: Performance Open Wheel Racing, Inc.
scope: regional/national dirt midgets, 410/305 sprints, micros
notes: National Midget League from 2004 (Gateway Racing Midget Series 2004-05), West Midget 2012, 410 Outlaw Sprint 2022; founded by promoter Kenny Brown.

name: Quarter Midgets of America
scope: national youth quarter midget sanction (club tracks)
notes: Ages 5-16 (rulebook allows up to 17); Honda 120 novice class; founding year not verified.

name: ROK Cup USA (Vortex ROK promoter)
scope: national one-engine karting promoter
notes: Promotes Florida Winter Tour, ROK Cup national events and qualifiers for ROK Vegas and the ROK Superfinal (Italy). Founding year not verified.

name: Southern All Star Dirt Racing Series
scope: regional Southeast super dirt late model tour
notes: Described as the longest-running dirt late model tour in America; new ownership Nov 2024.

name: Sports Car Club of America
scope: national amateur club racing (regional, Majors/Super Tour, Runoffs), autocross, rally; pro arm SCCA Pro Racing
notes: Largest US amateur road-racing club. Licensing ladder: Novice Permit (age 14+) -> driver school credit + 3 successful regional weekends -> Full Competition License (required for Majors/Super Tour/Runoffs). Created Trans-Am (1966). SCCA Enterprises builds spec cars (Spec Racer Ford, FE2). ACCUS member club.

name: SCCA Pro Racing
scope: national pro sanctioning arm of SCCA
notes: Formed 1963; sanctioned Trans-Am 1966-2006, World Challenge (1990-2010s), the Atlantic Championship revival (2012-), F1600/F2000 Championship Series; today sanctions F4 U.S. and Formula Regional Americas (with ACCUS for FIA status).

name: Skip Barber Racing School
scope: national racing school and entry-level series promoter
notes: Founded 1975, 400k+ students; Barber (Dodge) Pro Series 1986-2003; Skip Barber Formula Race Series continues; also runs arrive-and-drive programs (incl. a 2024 Pilot Challenge program).

name: Superkarts! USA
scope: national sprint karting (Pro Tour, Winter Series, SuperNationals)
notes: Runs the SuperNationals in Las Vegas since Nov 1997 (largest NA karting event, 400+ drivers) and the national Pro Tour; membership USD 150 initial/100 renewal. Alliance with IKF (2018). Founding year not verified (pre-1997).

name: SRO Motorsports America
scope: national pro/pro-am GT and touring promoter (USAC-sanctioned)
notes: Stephane Ratel Organisation took majority ownership of World Challenge in May 2018; runs GT World Challenge America, GT4 America, GT America, TC America, McLaren Trophy America and promotes Toyota GR Cup on its weekends. Classes use FIA driver categorisation (Pro/Pro-Am/Am, Silver).

name: UMP (United Midwestern Promoters, part of DIRTcar)
scope: weekly + regional Midwest dirt (late models, modifieds, Pro Late Model crate, Sportsman)
notes: Integrated into DIRTcar; UMP Modified ~750+hp 420ci, UMP Pro Late Model crate 602/604. Founding year not verified this session.

name: United States Auto Club
scope: national; oval midget/sprint/Silver Crown plus sanctioning of road-racing series run by promoters
notes: Sanctioned Indy/Champ cars until CART split (1979); ran the professional USAC Road Racing Championship 1958-1962; today sanctions the USF Pro Championships, SRO America series (GT World Challenge America, GT4 America, TC America; since 2017) and Porsche Sprint Challenge NA. ACCUS member club.

name: US Legend Cars International (manufacturer)
scope: manufacturer of Legends, Bandolero, Thunder Roadster
notes: Manufacturer, sanction via INEX. Founding year general knowledge (low).

name: United States Modified Touring Series
scope: national/regional dirt modified tour (Midwest, South, Plains)
notes: 48 nights in 2024; champion $100k.

name: United States Pro Kart Series
scope: national karting promoter (east/midwest)
notes: Founded 2013 by Mark Coats; inaugural event Mooresville NC.

name: United States Racing Association
scope: weekly dirt sanction (Midwest, Plains, South)
notes: Classes: Modified, B-Mod, Limited Mod, Late Model, Stock Car, Factory Stock, Hobby Stock, Tuners; grew from 28 tracks (2018) to 50+ (2022). Founding year not verified.

name: World Karting Association
scope: national karting (sprint, road-race/enduro, dirt/speedway)
notes: Founded 1971 (Kugler family) as east-coast alternative to IKF; based in Concord NC behind Charlotte Motor Speedway; 50k+ members since founding; Manufacturers Cup national sprint series. F4 U.S. Karting Alliance partner.

name: World Racing Group (World of Outlaws / DIRTcar)
scope: national tours + regional + weekly track sanction (DIRTcar, UMP)
notes: World of Outlaws founded 1978 (sprints); also WoO Late Models, Super DIRTcar Series (owned since 2003), DIRTcar UMP late models/modifieds, Xtreme DIRTcar. Founding year refers to WoO sprints.
